question: Why does possible untruth in authorities prevent certainty across different contexts?
premises: Even trusted authorities may be untruthful in some cases
Untruthfulness in one context undermines universal reliability
Without universal reliability certainty cannot be established
inference: Certainty cannot be secured if authorities may be untruthful elsewhere
plain_english: Even a father or others may be untruthful in one case, so there is no certainty that they are truthful elsewhere.
